# deezy temp

DeeZy keeps each input's temp files in a job folder under the platform's application data folder; `--temp-dir` moves them. These commands show and clean those folders.

<!-- BEGIN generated by scripts/cli_docs.py: edit the parsers in deezy/cli, not this block -->

```text {.scrollable-code-block}
usage: DeeZy temp [-h] {clean,info} ...

positional arguments:
  {clean,info}
    clean       Clean DeeZy temp folders
    info        Show temp folder information

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
```

## deezy temp clean

```text {.scrollable-code-block}
usage: DeeZy temp clean [-h] [--max-age HOURS] [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --max-age HOURS  Remove folders older than N hours (default: 24)
  --dry-run        Show what would be deleted without actually deleting
```

## deezy temp info

```text {.scrollable-code-block}
usage: DeeZy temp info [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

<!-- END generated -->

## Examples

- Show the temp folder and its size:

```bash
deezy temp info
```

- Show what cleaning would remove, without removing it:

```bash
deezy temp clean --max-age 24 --dry-run
```
